zoe.sales: Quick hit for CorpX sec team: need short guidance — should they do VPC peering or PrivateLink for an LLM private POC, exact firewall lines, and a single-line cost note for the RFP.

peter.net: Recommend PrivateLink for isolation. It prevents route-table exposure and makes allowlisting predictable. Use peering only if you need raw IP reachability between subnets.

hao.platform: Pasteable firewall rules (PrivateLink):
- Outbound TCP 443 -> <interface-endpoint-private-ips> (we will provide 3-4 per region)
- Optional UDP 123 -> internal NTP
Note: if you use a corporate TLS-inspecting proxy, configure TLS passthrough for these IPs to avoid breaking mTLS/cert pinning.

sam.security: Short RFP line: "We recommend AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for isolated POCs. Customers incur AWS interface-endpoint hourly and per-GB charges; standard cloud egress applies for NAT/proxy paths. Redwood can include data-transfer in Dedicated/Private quotes on request."

hao.platform: Add operational note: if routing via an egress proxy or NAT, the source IP seen by Redwood may be the proxy/NAT IP (SNAT). This affects source-ip-based allowlists and per-tenant IP preservation. If you require original src-IP, preserve it at the proxy or use PrivateLink.

peter.net: SNAT port exhaustion—short advice: use connection reuse (HTTP/2 or keepalive), increase NAT IPs or NAT gateways, or use multiple AZs for NATs for high-concurrency tests. We can provide concurrency-to-ephemeral-port guidance.

sam.security: For the questionnaire include these security bullets: support for customer-managed KMS for Private Deploys, SOC2/ISO artifacts available, cert thumbprints for endpoint validation, and optional mTLS for connector auth (we exchange certs during onboarding).

infra-bot: Ticket INF-9099 created to provision PrivateLink endpoints and will post the assigned private IPs to this thread when complete.

zoe.sales: Great — I'll send this combined reply and request a network contact for an ATO diagram. Thanks everyone!
